s0101.literal: At that time the district was desolate and refugees did not return; Cha lightened taxes and labor and urged farming, whereupon households flourished and the people still praise him today.
s0101.idiomatic: The district was desolate and refugees would not return; Cha eased taxes and labor and urged farming, and households soon flourished—the people still praise him today.

s0102.literal: Du Zhiwei, Vice Director of the Secretariat who concurrently headed the Directorate of History, was deeply fond of him; he memorialized to employ Cha as assistant in the directorate, and Cha continued composing history.
s0102.idiomatic: Du Zhiwei, vice director of the secretariat who also headed the directorate of history, was deeply attached to him; he memorialized to appoint Cha as an assistant compiler, and Cha went on writing history.

s0103.literal: At the beginning of Yongding he was appointed Records Officer of the Princedom of Shixing; soon he was made an academic of the Hall of Illustrious Virtue and transferred to Recorder of the Princedom of Shixing under Central Guard and Pillar of State.
s0103.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongding he was made records officer of the princedom of Shixing; soon he became an academic of the Hall of Illustrious Virtue, then recorder of the princedom of Shixing under central guard and pillar of state.

s0104.literal: Xu Ling, Minister of Personnel, then concurrently headed the directorate; he again recruited Cha as a history assistant, and when Ling's memorials declining office and retiring were all drafted, Cha was asked to compose them; Ling sighed and said, "I do not match him."
s0104.idiomatic: Xu Ling, minister of personnel, was then also in charge of the history office and again took Cha on as a history assistant; when Ling's memorials declining office and seeking retirement were drafted, Cha wrote them all. Ling sighed, "I cannot equal him."

s0105.literal: Early in the Taichu era he was made an academic of the Hall of Bright Illumination and appointed Vice Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and Left Direct Communicator.
s0105.idiomatic: Early in Taichu he was made an academic of the Hall of Bright Illumination and appointed vice attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and left direct communicator.

s0106.literal: Soon he was concurrently Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry for Direct Communication and sent as envoy on a return mission to Zhou.
s0106.idiomatic: Soon he was also regular attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry for direct communication and sent on a return mission to Zhou.

s0107.literal: Elders of the southeast already in the Guan region all admired him.
s0107.idiomatic: Elders of the southeast already living in the Guan region all admired him.

s0108.literal: Liu Zhen of Pei privately at the embassy lodge asked over ten doubtful points in the Book of Han; Cha analyzed them all, each with textual basis.
s0108.idiomatic: Liu Zhen of Pei privately came to the embassy lodge and asked more than ten doubtful points in the Book of Han; Cha explained them all with solid textual grounds.

s0109.literal: Zhen told his intimates, "When a reputation is settled, there is no empty scholar."
s0109.idiomatic: Zhen told those close to him, "A settled reputation never rests on an empty scholar."

s0110.literal: He wrote the Record of Roads on the Western Mission; the matters he narrated were very detailed.
s0110.idiomatic: He wrote the Record of Roads on the Western Mission, narrating the journey in great detail.

s0111.literal: When the mission returned, he was made an academic of the Eastern Palace.
s0111.idiomatic: On his return from the mission he was made an eastern palace academic.

s0112.literal: At that time Jiang Zong of Jiyang, Gu Yewang of Wu, Lu Qiong, his cousin Yu, Chu Zhi of Henan, Fu Zai of Beidi, and others all for literary talent were morning and evening companions in entertainment.
s0112.idiomatic: At that time Jiang Zong of Jiyang, Gu Yewang of Wu, Lu Qiong, his cousin Yu, Chu Zhi of Henan, Fu Zai of Beidi, and others—all famed for learning—served the heir morning and evening as literary companions.

s0113.literal: In every discourse and composition Cha was revered by them all.
s0113.idiomatic: Whatever Cha said or wrote, the others held in high regard.

s0114.literal: The heir was deeply courteous beyond the other officials; whatever manuscript the palace needed was entrusted to Cha for immediate drafting.
s0114.idiomatic: The crown prince treated him with exceptional courtesy; whatever the palace needed in writing was sent to Cha to draft on the spot.

s0115.literal: He was repeatedly ordered to debate in turn with Gu Yewang and always won reward and praise.
s0115.idiomatic: He was often ordered to question Gu Yewang in turn and always won praise and rewards.

s0116.literal: He was moved to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites for Sacrificial Affairs.
s0116.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the ministry of rites for sacrificial affairs.

s0117.literal: This bureau oversaw suburban altars; in the past Wei Wang Su memorialized on sacrificing to Heaven and Earth, establishing palace music and eight rows of dancers, and afterward custom was followed without change.
s0117.idiomatic: That bureau oversaw suburban altars. Once Wang Su of Wei had memorialized on sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, setting up palace music and eight rows of dancers; afterward the practice was followed unchanged.

s0118.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang held that rites for men were elaborate and rites for gods simple, and that antiquity had no text for palace music.
s0118.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang held that rites toward men should be elaborate and rites toward the gods simple, and that antiquity had no precedent for palace music.

s0119.literal: At the beginning of Chen they continued the practice without change.
s0119.idiomatic: When Chen was founded the court kept the practice as it was.

s0120.literal: Emperor Gaozong wished to prepare full music and charged the offices to debate, holding Liang Wu in the wrong.
s0120.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong wanted full ritual music and ordered the offices to debate, taking Liang Wu to have been mistaken.

s0121.literal: Then eminent scholars and worthies at court all hoped for the emperor's intent and immediately noted agreement.
s0121.idiomatic: Leading scholars and officials at court all read the emperor's mind and at once sided with him.

s0122.literal: Cha broadly cited the classics, alone opposed the group, and held Liang music correct; all were startled and ashamed into assent, and Director Xu Ling then changed to Cha's view.
s0122.idiomatic: Cha cited the classics at length, stood alone against the consensus, and argued that Liang music was right. The court was astonished and ashamed into agreement; Director Xu Ling then adopted Cha's position.

s0123.literal: His refusal to follow the times and fashion were all of this kind.
s0123.idiomatic: His refusal to bend to fashion was always of this sort.

s0124.literal: He was appointed Central Recorder of the Princedom of Yidu under Splendid Favor, concurrently an eastern palace academic.
s0124.idiomatic: He was made central recorder of the princedom of Yidu under splendid favor, while retaining his eastern palace academic post.

s0125.literal: He served as consulting colonel for the princes of Huainan and Jian'an and left office on mourning for his mother.
s0125.idiomatic: He served as consulting colonel to the princes of Huainan and Jian'an, then left office to mourn his mother.

s0126.literal: Soon he was recalled as Rongzhao general and charged with compiling the history of Liang; he firmly declined but could not escape.
s0126.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as rongzhao general and put in charge of compiling the history of Liang; he pleaded hard to be excused but could not.

s0127.literal: When Houzhu succeeded to the throne he ordered Cha concurrently Eastern Palace Communicating Affairs Attendant; his generalship and charge over history remained as before.
s0127.idiomatic: When Houzhu took the throne he ordered Cha to serve concurrently as eastern palace communicating affairs attendant; his general's rank and charge over history stayed the same.

s0128.literal: He was also ordered to specialize in posthumous titles, eulogies, and such writing.
s0128.idiomatic: He was also ordered to handle posthumous titles, eulogies, and similar court writings.

s0129.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, then Steward of the Heir Apparent; the rest remained as before.
s0129.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhide he was made vice director of the secretariat, then steward of the heir apparent; his other posts were unchanged.

s0130.literal: Earlier, when the Liang age fell, his father Sengyuan went to Chang'an; Cha ate only vegetables and wore plain cloth and heard no music; now news of his death came via the envoys to the south.
s0130.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liang fell, his father Sengyuan had gone to Chang'an. Cha lived on vegetables and plain cloth and would not hear music. Now word of his father's death reached the south with the returning envoys.

s0131.literal: Cha's mother Lady Wei had just ended her mourning period; Houzhu, seeing Cha emaciated, feared he would collapse further and secretly sent Secretariat Attendant Sima Shen to initiate mourning at his home, ordering Shen specially to admonish restraint.
s0131.idiomatic: Cha's mother, Lady Wei, had just left mourning. Houzhu, seeing how wasted Cha was, feared he would ruin his health and secretly sent secretariat attendant Sima Shen to begin mourning rites at his house, with orders to counsel restraint.

s0132.literal: Later he again sent Shen with an edict of admonition, saying: "Knowing that your grief exceeds the rites, I am very concerned.
s0132.idiomatic: Later he again sent Shen with an edict of admonition: "I know your mourning goes beyond the rites, and I am deeply troubled.

s0133.literal: You stand alone; the clan sacrifices rest on you; to destroy yourself and annihilate your nature is what the sage teaching does not permit.
s0133.idiomatic: You stand alone, and the clan sacrifices depend on you. To ruin yourself is what the sages forbid.

s0134.literal: You should slightly restrain yourself to preserve the ritual order.
s0134.idiomatic: You should restrain yourself a little and keep within the rites.

s0135.literal: My worry being deep, hence this message."
s0135.idiomatic: My concern is great, and so I send you this word."

s0136.literal: Soon he was recalled as Zhongyi general, concurrently Eastern Palace Communicating Affairs Attendant.
s0136.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as zhongyi general and again made eastern palace communicating affairs attendant.

s0137.literal: Cha wished to complete the full mourning period and repeatedly memorialized, but each plea was suppressed and denied.
s0137.idiomatic: Cha wished to observe the full mourning term and memorialized again and again, but each request was refused.

s0138.literal: He also submitted a memorial in gist, saying: "My family has suffered calamity and met punishment together; stealing days I hoped to fulfill feeling and rite, yet sicknesses follow one upon another, my straw mat and unclean body—no longer among men, about to finish the mourning hut."
s0138.idiomatic: He also submitted a summary memorial: "My household has met calamity and punishment together. I have clung to life day by day only to fulfill feeling and rite, yet sickness follows sickness; on my straw mat, an unclean body no longer fit for human company, I am about to finish my time in the mourning hut."

s0139.literal: How could I expect court grace bent so wide, crowned with cap and sash; receiving such favor only deepens my shame.
s0139.idiomatic: How could I expect the court's grace to bend so far as to crown me with cap and sash? Such favor only deepens my shame.

s0140.literal: The palace secrets are profound and attendance is frequent—how can one in such ruined mourning presume to take part?
s0140.idiomatic: The palace is secret and business urgent—how can one so broken by mourning presume to attend?

s0141.literal: I bow and wish Your supreme virtue and filial rule to pity this seizure of feeling and let my broken soul breathe to finish my remaining life."
s0141.idiomatic: I beg Your supreme virtue and filial government to pity this conflict of feeling and duty and let my shattered spirit recover enough to live out what remains."

s0142.literal: The edict replied: "Your memorial is received with understanding.
s0142.idiomatic: The edict answered: "Your memorial has been read and understood.

s0143.literal: Your conduct is deep and pure and your fame long bright; you yield to feeling and rite and are not yet fit for the brush.
s0143.idiomatic: Your conduct is deep and pure and your reputation long established; you are yielding to feeling and rite and are not yet fit for office.

s0144.literal: But service at Chenghua is well hoped for; grant this restraint of mourning—you may not decline."
s0144.idiomatic: Yet service at Chenghua is what the court expects of you. Allow this shortening of mourning—you may not refuse."

s0145.literal: Soon he was ordered to oversee the duties of Director of History; when mourning ended he was made Attending Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently heading the directorate.
s0145.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to oversee the directorate of history. When mourning ended he was made attending gentleman of the Yellow Gate, still in charge of the history office.

s0146.literal: Cha had long been in mourning and fasting; after mourning ended he developed a breath illness.
s0146.idiomatic: Cha had long been in mourning and on a plain diet; after mourning ended he developed a chronic breathing ailment.

s0147.literal: Houzhu once summoned him separately, saw him gaunt beyond measure, was moved, and said to Cha: "The court values you; you should value yourself—having eaten vegetables so long, you may stop the perpetual fast."
s0147.idiomatic: Houzhu once summoned him privately, saw how wasted he was, and was moved. He told Cha, "The court values you; value yourself. You have eaten only vegetables for years—you may end the long fast."

s0148.literal: He also sent Minister of Revenue Wang Yuan with an edict to comfort him again and allow an evening meal.
s0148.idiomatic: He also sent minister of revenue Wang Yuan with an edict to comfort him again and permit an evening meal.

s0149.literal: A hand edict said: "You are so emaciated and have fasted for years; one meal a day harms recovery; if you follow this, it will be excellent."
s0149.idiomatic: A handwritten edict said, "You are so thin, and you have fasted for years. One meal a day is bad for your recovery. If you do as I say, that will be best."

s0150.literal: Though Cha obeyed the edict, he still kept his old vow.
s0150.idiomatic: Cha received the order, but still held to his old vow.

s0151.literal: He was again ordered Secretary Supervisor, with the history post unchanged; he advanced refusal again and again, and each time the gracious reply denied him.
s0151.idiomatic: He was again made secretary supervisor while keeping charge of history. He memorialized refusal repeatedly, and each time the gracious reply refused him.

s0152.literal: At the Secretariat he greatly revised and corrected texts and also memorialized to compile the Collection of Secretariat Memorials.
s0152.idiomatic: At the secretariat he made extensive revisions and also memorialized to compile a collection of secretariat memorials.

s0153.literal: He was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; soon Minister of Revenue; within a month Minister of Personnel, with the history post unchanged.
s0153.idiomatic: He was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, soon minister of revenue, and within a month minister of personnel, still heading the history office.

s0154.literal: Cha had thoroughly mastered the classics and was especially skilled at persons—from the origins of surnames, branches divided, offices and marriages, rise and fall—discussing all without omission.
s0154.idiomatic: Cha had mastered the classics and was especially skilled with people: surname origins, family branches, offices and marriages, rise and fall—he could discuss them all without omission.

s0155.literal: Men had long compared the clarifying-mirror post to a master carpenter; on moving to the selection bureau he fully met the court's hopes.
s0155.idiomatic: For years men had likened the clarifying-mirror office to a master carpenter's work; when he moved to the selection bureau he fully satisfied court expectations.

s0156.literal: When Minister of Personnel Cai Zheng moved to Secretariat Director, Houzhu was choosing his successor; Director Jiang Zong and others all recommended Cha; the edict answered: "Yao Cha is not only learned and broad but his conduct is pure and cultivated; the post of selection is hard to fill—we have him now."
s0156.idiomatic: When minister of personnel Cai Zheng was moved to secretariat director, Houzhu had to choose a successor. Director Jiang Zong and others all recommended Cha. The edict answered, "Yao Cha is not only learned and broad; his conduct is pure and cultivated. The post of selection is hard to fill, and now we have found the man."

s0157.literal: Then with the imperial brush he drafted the edict [8] and read it to Cha; Cha declined urgently.
s0157.idiomatic: Then with the imperial brush he drafted the edict and read it to Cha, who declined with great urgency.

s0158.literal: On another day he was summoned to discuss selection; Cha, weeping, bowed and pleaded: "I am of a low clan of the eastern marshes; my talent is mediocre, my ambition forgets far reach, my thoughts cut off the path of cultivation.
s0158.idiomatic: On another day he was summoned to discuss appointments. Cha wept as he bowed and pleaded, "I am a humble clan of the eastern marshes; my talent is slight, my ambition forgets distant goals, my mind has turned from self-cultivation.

s0159.literal: Recently holding office beyond measure, I have long known it exceeds my place, only because the eastern palace drew me up and favor was wrongly added.
s0159.idiomatic: For some time I have held office beyond my measure and long known it exceeds my place, only because the eastern palace drew me up and favor was wrongly heaped on me.

s0160.literal: Today's appointment is not from talent; even if Your Majesty specially raises this mediocrity, what of court order?"
s0160.idiomatic: Today's appointment is not from merit. Even if Your Majesty specially raises this mediocrity, what becomes of court order?"

s0161.literal: My ninth-generation ancestor Xin was famed in a past age and barely held the selection bureau—since then few have followed.
s0161.idiomatic: My ninth-generation ancestor Xin was famed in a past age and barely held the selection bureau; since then few in our line have followed him.

s0162.literal: I met with promotion, bathed in grace, repeatedly received unfitting posts, and each time harmed worthies.
s0162.idiomatic: I have met with promotion, bathed in grace, repeatedly received posts beyond my worth, and each time blocked better men.

s0163.literal: Though without insight I know myself; in conduct I never hoped for glory—how could I expect the weight of balancing to be wrongly given a non-talent?"
s0163.idiomatic: Though I lack insight I know myself. In conduct I never hoped for glory—how could I expect the weight of selection to be wrongly placed on a man without talent?"

s0164.literal: Moreover Your bright rule towers over past ages; feathered guards and famed ministers in the inner councils—if appointment is fitting, that is competence.
s0164.idiomatic: Moreover Your bright rule towers above past ages. Feathered guards and famed ministers fill the inner councils—if appointments are rightly made, that is true competence.

s0165.literal: I have long been steeped in teaching and know surely it cannot be."
s0165.idiomatic: I have long been steeped in teaching and know this cannot be."

s0166.literal: Houzhu said: "Choosing the masses is what all agree on. Once Mao Jie was refined and pure, Lu Yu level and upright, Wang Yun balanced in measure, and Shan Tao chose without losing talent—from you we seek all this.
s0166.idiomatic: Houzhu said, "Choosing the right men is what everyone expects. Once Mao Jie was refined and pure, Lu Yu level and upright, Wang Yun balanced in judgment, and Shan Tao chose without losing talent—from you we expect all of this.

s0167.literal: Moreover, though lord and minister are apart in ritual, our feeling is unusually close; the mirror of mankind is well entrusted to you—you need not shame the exemplars."
s0167.idiomatic: And though lord and minister stand apart in ritual, our bond is unusual. The mirror of mankind is what I entrust to you—you need not shame those exemplars."

s0168.literal: Since holding high office Cha greatly urged purity; beyond salary and gifts he had no contact whatever.
s0168.idiomatic: Once in high office Cha strove for purity. Beyond salary and imperial gifts he had no dealings with anyone.

s0169.literal: Once a private student dared not give a lavish gift and sent only one bolt of southern cloth and one bolt of patterned silk.
s0169.idiomatic: Once a private student, not daring a lavish gift, sent only one bolt of southern cloth and one bolt of patterned silk.

s0170.literal: [10] Cha told him: "What I wear is only hemp and rush silk—these are useless to me.
s0170.idiomatic: Cha told him, "What I wear is only hemp and rush silk. These things are useless to me.

s0171.literal: If you wish friendship, please do not trouble with these."
s0171.idiomatic: If you wish friendship, please do not trouble yourself with such gifts."

s0172.literal: The man humbly pleaded, still hoping for acceptance; Cha sternly drove him out [11]; hence servants dared not offer gifts.
s0172.idiomatic: The man humbly pleaded, still hoping Cha would accept; Cha sternly drove him out. After that, those who served him dared not offer gifts.

s0173.literal: When Chen fell he entered Sui; in the ninth year of Kaihuang he was ordered Secretariat Assistant, with a separate edict to complete the histories of Liang and Chen.
s0173.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered Sui. In the ninth year of Kaihuang he was made secretariat assistant, with a separate edict to complete the histories of Liang and Chen.

s0174.literal: He was also ordered to attend long at Zhuhua Pavilion.
s0174.idiomatic: He was also ordered to attend regularly at Zhuhua Pavilion.

s0175.literal: Emperor Wen knew Cha's vegetarian diet; one day he alone summoned him to the inner hall, gave him fruit and vegetables, and pointing to Cha told the court: "I hear Yao Cha's learning and conduct are unmatched today; in pacifying Chen I gained only this one man."
s0175.idiomatic: Emperor Wen knew Cha lived on vegetables. One day he summoned him alone to the inner hall, gave him fruit and vegetables, and pointing to Cha told the court, "I hear Yao Cha's learning and conduct are unmatched today. In pacifying Chen I gained only this one man."

s0176.literal: In the thirteenth year he inherited the title Duke of Beijiang commandery.
s0176.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he inherited the title duke of Beijiang commandery.

s0177.literal: When Cha went as envoy to Zhou he had been able to meet his father Sengyuan; on parting he fainted and revived; now inheriting the title his grief grew deeper, and all who saw him wept.
s0177.idiomatic: When Cha went as envoy to Zhou he had met his father Sengyuan; on parting he had fainted and revived. Now, on inheriting the title, his grief grew keener, and all who saw him sighed.

s0178.literal: In youth at Mingqing Temple on Zhongshan he received bodhisattva precepts from Master Shang; in Chen office all salary was given to temple construction, and he also erected a stele for the master, the text very forceful.
s0178.idiomatic: In youth he had received bodhisattva precepts at Mingqing Temple on Zhongshan from Master Shang. In Chen office he gave all his salary to temple building and later erected a stele for the master in forceful prose.

s0179.literal: Now, finding Director of the National University Xiao Ziyun's chan poetry for the temple, reading it moved him to compose in Xiao's rhyme; the words were very mournful, and clerics and laity praised him the more.
s0179.idiomatic: Now he came upon the chan poetry that Xiao Ziyun, director of the national university, had written for the temple. Reading it moved him to compose in Xiao's rhyme; the words were very mournful, and monks and laymen praised him all the more.

s0180.literal: He mourned his stepmother Lady Du and left office.
s0180.idiomatic: He mourned his stepmother, Lady Du, and left office.

s0181.literal: During the mourning period a white dove nested above the door.
s0181.idiomatic: During mourning a white dove nested above his door.

s0182.literal: At seventy-four, in the second year of Daye, he died in the Eastern Capital; his testament ordered a plain burial, with utmost simplicity.
s0182.idiomatic: At seventy-four, in the second year of Daye, he died in the eastern capital. His testament ordered a plain burial, kept as simple as possible.

s0183.literal: In gist it said: "Our house for generations has been plain scholars and has fixed custom.
s0183.idiomatic: In gist it said, "Our house has been plain scholars for generations and has its fixed custom.

s0184.literal: I wish burial garb by law, all of cloth, with earth to the body.
s0184.idiomatic: I wish to be dressed for burial according to law, all in cloth, with earth heaped only to the body.

s0185.literal: Fearing you cannot bear this—if not, then pine boards and a thin coffin barely enclosing the body, with earth only around the coffin.
s0185.idiomatic: Fearing you cannot bear this—if you cannot, then use pine boards and a thin coffin barely large enough for the body, with earth only around the coffin.

s0186.literal: On the burial day only a rough cart; send me to the old tomb to the north.
s0186.idiomatic: On the burial day use only a rough cart and send me to the old tomb to the north.

s0187.literal: In the Liang age, when I was fourteen, I took precepts at Mingqing Temple on Zhongshan from Master Shang; since then I deeply knew the emptiness of suffering and somewhat understood turning dedication.
s0187.idiomatic: In Liang, at fourteen, I took precepts at Mingqing Temple on Zhongshan from Master Shang. Since then I have deeply known the emptiness of suffering and somewhat understood turning merit toward others.

s0188.literal: Once I lingered at a mountain temple and went away forgetting to return.
s0188.idiomatic: Once I lingered at a mountain temple and went away, forgetting to return.

s0189.literal: Serving Chen, famous men granted me reputation, and with the ruler's favor my office reached prominence.
s0189.idiomatic: Serving Chen, famous men granted me reputation, and with the ruler's favor my office rose to prominence.

s0190.literal: Since entering court I have again received thick grace.
s0190.idiomatic: Since entering court I have again received generous favor.

s0191.literal: Bound to the human world, my original aim was not followed.
s0191.idiomatic: Bound to the human world, my original aim was not fulfilled.

s0192.literal: Moreover I have practiced vegetarianism for fifty-odd years and through the years kept it without lapse.
s0192.idiomatic: Moreover I have eaten only vegetables for more than fifty years and kept to it through the years without lapse.

s0193.literal: After closing my eyes do not set up a spirit tablet; place a small bed and daily set out clear water; on the six fast days set out vegetarian fruit—as the household has, without special provision.
s0193.idiomatic: After I close my eyes do not set up a spirit tablet. Place a small bed and each day set out clear water. On the six fast days set out vegetarian fruit—as the household can afford, without special arrangements.

s0194.literal: Earlier Cha had wished to read the whole canon and had completed it; at the end he had no pain, only sat facing west in right mindfulness, saying, "All is empty and still."
s0194.idiomatic: Earlier Cha had wished to read the whole canon through and had finished it. At the end he felt no pain, only sat facing west in right mindfulness and said, "All is empty and still."

s0195.literal: Afterward his body was soft and his color as usual.
s0195.idiomatic: Afterward his body remained soft and his color unchanged.

s0196.literal: Both palaces mourned him and funeral gifts were very rich.
s0196.idiomatic: Both palaces mourned him and sent very rich funeral gifts.

s0197.literal: Cha by nature was utmost in filial piety and had discernment in human relations.
s0197.idiomatic: By nature Cha was deeply filial and had a keen eye for human relations.

s0198.literal: Modest and humble, he never flaunted his strengths.
s0198.idiomatic: Modest and humble, he never flaunted what he knew.

s0199.literal: All day tranquil, he took books alone as joy—in the classics there was nothing he had not read.
s0199.idiomatic: Tranquil all day, he took books alone as his pleasure; in the classics there was nothing he had not read.

s0200.literal: In every composition he used novelty unseen before, and all valued his richness.
s0200.idiomatic: In every piece he wrote he favored what was new and unseen, and all prized his breadth.
